title: Why tests and monitors catch different failures
meta_description: Hand-written data tests cover known rules. Monitors cover the failures nobody wrote a test for. Here is how to use both.
body_markdown:
Data teams that bill millions of customers cannot afford a wrong number reaching an invoice.

## Tests cover the rules you know

Code-defined testing tools let engineers write a test for each table. [E8] That works well for rules you already understand.

## Monitors cover the rest

A monitor watches every table for schema drift, staleness and volume anomalies, and alerts the owning team within five minutes. [E1] Regulators also expect utilities to document the controls behind billing data. [E9]

## Use both

Run tests for known rules and monitors for everything else. A regional water company cut triage from six hours to ninety minutes this way. [E2]
